category: a proxy written in Rust on Cloudflare's Pingora framework - routing and policies as code
notes: A ~700-line Rust proxy on Pingora 0.9 (Cloudflare's framework): ProxyHttp hooks implement host/path routing, round-robin / weighted / ketama hashing / cookie stickiness, HTTP health checks, retries on connect failure, outlier ejection, h2c and verified-TLS upstreams, gRPC, rate and concurrency limits (pingora-limits), JWT (jsonwebtoken), basic auth, IP lists, fault injection, per-route timeouts, response cache (pingora-cache MemCache), compression, mTLS, SNI certificate callback, a static file, a custom error page, JSON access log, Prometheus metrics, a status API and a raw TCP proxy app. Zero-downtime upgrade via the framework's socket hand-off. What is missing is missing from the code, not from the framework's limits (mostly).

unsupported.lb_least_conn: pingora-load-balancing ships round-robin / random / consistent-hash selection; least-connections would be a custom BackendSelection
unsupported.lb_mirror: no mirroring in the framework (would be a second upstream request written by hand)
unsupported.tls_passthrough_sni: the L4 app in this proxy copies bytes; SNI parsing for passthrough is not implemented
unsupported.acme_auto_cert: no ACME client (certificates come from files / callbacks)
unsupported.cache_purge: pingora-cache serves PURGE only for storages implementing purge; MemCache does in principle but the lab keeps it out of scope
unsupported.cache_stale_on_error: stale-if-error is wired through should_serve_stale(); the in-memory cache expires objects before the lab's 2 s window
unsupported.compress_brotli: pingora's compression module in this build negotiates gzip/zstd (brotli support is feature-gated)
unsupported.forward_auth: no built-in subrequest to an authorizer (would be a hand-written upstream call)
unsupported.bandwidth_limit: no built-in bandwidth limiting (body filters are synchronous)
unsupported.tracing_otel: no OpenTelemetry integration in this binary
